text:
meera: Quick Q — I'm hitting AccessDenied when a pod tries to KMS Decrypt after switching this service to IRSA. Pushed a tiny TF change, not sure what I missed.

meera: Relevant bits: 
```hcl
resource "aws_iam_role" "app_sa_role" {
  name = "app-sa-role"
  assume_role_policy = jsonencode({
    Version = "2012-10-17"
    Statement = [{
      Effect = "Allow"
      Principal = { Federated = aws_iam_openid_connect_provider.eks.arn }
      Action = "sts:AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity"
      Condition = { StringEquals = { "oidc.eks.region.amazonaws.com/id/EXAMPLE:sub" = "system:serviceaccount:prod:app-sa" } }
    }]
  })
}

resource "aws_kms_grant" "app_sa_grant" {
  key_id = aws_kms_key.app_key.key_id
  grantee_principal = aws_iam_role.app_sa_role.arn
  operations = ["Decrypt"]
}

# k8s sa annotation: 
# eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn: ${aws_iam_role.app_sa_role.arn}
```

meera: Pod logs show: 
`User: arn:aws:sts::123456789012:assumed-role/app-sa-role/AWSALBIngressController is not authorized to perform: kms:Decrypt`

alejandro: A few quick checks:
- Confirm the KMS key policy allows the role ARN (or the account) to use the key. KMS checks key policy first. If you only created a grant, but key policy denies, Decrypt still fails.
- For IRSA the principal that performs the call is the assumed-role session principal (arn:aws:sts::acct:assumed-role/role-name/session-name). Grants accept the role ARN as grantee_principal but the key policy needs to let the assumed session in or allow the role.
- Also check the grant actually exists / wasn't created in a different account or deleted by CI cleanup.

tim: Small gotcha we've hit: if your key policy has a Condition restricting by `aws:PrincipalArn` exact match, it might not match the assumed-role session ARN. Prefer allowing the role ARN ("arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/app-sa-role") or use `StringLike` on `aws:PrincipalArn` to allow the assumed-role form.

alejandro: If you want to keep tight key policy, add something like: 
```json
{"Sid":"AllowIRSAApp", "Effect":"Allow","Principal":{"AWS":"arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/app-sa-role"},"Action":["kms:Decrypt","kms:Encrypt","kms:GenerateDataKey*"],"Resource":"*"}
```
Or in Terraform: add an aws_kms_key policy statement that references the role ARN.

meera: Hmm, our key policy currently uses an account principal and then a condition on `aws:PrincipalArn` expecting `arn:aws:sts::*:assumed-role/app-sa-role/*`. I probably messed up the wildcard.

tim: Also check the grant resource attributes: `grantee_principal` should be the role ARN, not the assumed-role ARN. And `operations = ["Decrypt"]`. If you rotate or re-create grants, older sessions lose access; grants are independent from key policy.

meera: Do I need both grant + key policy? I briefly removed the grant thinking key policy is enough.

alejandro: Key policy can be sufficient on its own. Grants are useful when you want to allow a principal in another account or to give temporary permissions without editing the key policy. But many infra setups use both. If the key policy allows the role, you don't strictly need a grant.

meera: Ok I'll: 1) fix the key policy statement to allow the role ARN (or StringLike on assumed-role), 2) ensure the TF aws_kms_grant uses the role ARN and operations include Decrypt, 3) re-deploy SA annotation and restart pods.

infra-bot: terraform plan for infra/app-service succeeded in workspace prod — changes: +1 to kms_grant, ~1 to kms_key policy

meera: Pushed a tiny fix to policy + grant, restarted pod, yes !app-service logs now show successful Decrypt. Thanks both. :tada:

tim: Nice. Optional follow-up: add an integration test that runs a short decrypt in CI (assume IRSA role) so we catch policy/assume-role regressions earlier.

meera: Will do a quick CI job tomorrow and link it here. Thanks.
